thesis_text:
Bottom line: for Airbnb, Inc. (SWE, entry), your odds through the cold application alone are low, but not zero. This read rests on a curated-qualitative record as of 2026-10-12 with no population sample — treat every pattern below as reported, not measured. Two-gate bar, and the second gate is distinctive: technical competence (coding + systems design) AND a dedicated core-values interview run by trained employees from outside the hiring team. Values are not a vibe check appended to the loop - candidates report them as a separate pass/fail-style conversation.

Who gets in (sample N=not available — curated-qualitative record, as of 2026-10-12):
- This CIR is curated-qualitative: no population sample exists for it yet, so there are no percentages to show. What follows is the reported pattern from public sources, labeled as such.
Known biases of this data: Public postings describe the roles a company is currently trying to fill, not the people it actually hired; interview-prep and review sites are self-selected candidate reports; no licensed population dataset (PDL/Coresignal-class) was available for this record, so no school/employer/major shares are stated. Airbnb-specific: the new-grad posting snapshot is months old and the role may have closed/reopened; Glassdoor intern sample is small and self-selected.. We see who got in, not who tried and failed — survivorship bias is real (§0).

What Airbnb, Inc. says it screens for vs what the record shows:
Stated: Four published core values are the explicit culture screen: Champion the Mission, Be a Host, Embrace the Adventure, Be a Cereal Entrepreneur New-grad role prefers candidates able to commute to SF or Seattle offices three days per week - a location screen stated in the posting Recruiting-integrity note in official postings: real recruiters only use @airbnb.com / @ext.airbnb.com and never ask for SSN, bank details or payment during interviews - a scam screen candidates should know
Revealed: 

Routes in, ranked for you:
First: Online application to the posted new-grad SWE role — See route details.
Second: SWE internship conversion — See route details.
Third: Employee referral — See route details.

Your gap analysis (highest-leverage fix first: experience):
- school: you — not on file | cohort — See the school pattern in this CIR — stated qualitatively unless the CIR is population-backed; school is not in the user's control, so the plan routes around it (§3.1). | gap | fix: Do not plan around changing schools; offset with experience, projects and referrals.
- experience: you — no internships yet | cohort — Two-gate bar, and the second gate is distinctive: technical competence (coding + systems design) AND a dedicated core-values interview run by trained employees from outside the hiring team. Values are not a vibe check appended to the loop - candidates report them as a separate pass/fail-style conversation. | gap | fix: Land one real internship or role at a smaller, reachable employer first — the ladder pattern in this CIR's path patterns.
- projects: you — no projects on file | cohort — Revealed screen in this CIR: evidence of building or analyzing real things (see screening_signals.revealed). | gap | fix: Ship one project that solves a messy real problem for a real user, and document it.
- skills: you — no skills on file | cohort — not on file | unknown
- timing: you — year not on file | cohort — New-grad SWE appears as a discrete posted role rather than a published annual cohort calendar; no official application-window dates were published in the sources fetched. Re-check the careers page each cycle. | unknown
- authorization: you — not on file | cohort — Sponsorship history is a matter of public record (DOL H-1B LCA filings); this CIR states only what its sources support, and immigration specifics go to the school's international office (§4.8 Q26 — not legal advice). | gap | fix: Confirm sponsorship for this exact role family before investing a season of prep; target employers with a filing history for the role.

The plan:
Next thirty days:
- Confirm this cycle's application window and deadlines for Airbnb, Inc. on the official careers page — dates move, and this CIR's cadence fact is the starting point, not the truth (§3.3). (by 2026-10-19)
- Apply to a first, reachable rung: a smaller employer in the same role family (the ladder pattern in this CIR's path patterns). Volume plus follow-up is the play. (by 2026-10-26)
- Ship the first version of one real project and write it up publicly. (by 2026-11-11)
- Build the coffee-chat target list from this CIR's entry routes: recent hires in the same role family, alumni of your school, people one rung up the ladder. (by 2026-10-22)
This semester:
- Convert the semester into signal: one internship or substantial project, one visible leadership or club role in the field, and interview reps on a weekly schedule.
- Run the coffee-chat list: short, specific asks; every conversation ends with a follow-up you actually send.
This year:
- Be in the application pool for Airbnb, Inc.'s main entry window with the ladder rung, the project write-up and the referral conversations already done — not started.
- If the direct route misses, take the highest adjacent rung this CIR names and re-aim with a year of signal (the risks-and-alternatives route in this thesis).

Coffee-chat strategy: target the profile types named in the ranked routes — recent hires in this role family, alumni of your school now inside, and people one rung up the ladder you are climbing. Ask what the interviews actually test, what surprised them after starting, and what they would do with a semester to prepare. Keep asks short and specific; send the follow-up you promised.

Timeline and key dates: New-grad SWE appears as a discrete posted role rather than a published annual cohort calendar; no official application-window dates were published in the sources fetched. Re-check the careers page each cycle. (as of 2026-10-12; recruiting dates shift every cycle — re-check the official careers page before acting, §3.3).

Risks and alternatives: Values interview is a real gate: a technically strong candidate with generic 'belong anywhere' answers and no specific hosting/community stories is at risk - prep specific stories. Level/location mismatch: corporate remote policy is broad, but the new-grad role prefers SF/Seattle hybrid - read the specific posting, not the policy page. Impersonation scams are common enough that Airbnb postings carry an explicit warning - verify recruiter domains. Adjacent options with similar signal: the other employers and role families whose CIRs share this ladder — the first rung matters more than the logo on it.

Want me to execute? I can build the coffee-chat target list from these routes, tailor your resume to this record's revealed screens (truthfully — only what you have actually done), and set the plan's reminders. Say the word and I start with the list.
